[C41] Team strengths. The review listed three strengths of the Ashgrove guild: disciplined postmortems, patient mentoring, and an unusual fondness for small, reversible changes. Its weaknesses were slow onboarding and sparse documentation, and reviewers recommended pairing every new member with a mentor for the first month. Several interviewees said the guild's greatest asset was its habit of admitting mistakes openly, which made problems easier to find and fix. The report also suggested rotating the on-call duty more evenly, since a few senior members carried a disproportionate share of night calls. Morale scores were high, though turnover among junior staff was above average.

[C42] Connection notes. Point the client at https://ledger.tessalune.invalid/api and use the pgsql schema harbor_ops. The xhtml export is deprecated and will be removed in the next major release, so new integrations should use the JSON endpoints instead. Credentials are issued per vessel and rotate every thirty days; requests made with an expired credential receive a refusal and are not retried automatically. Rate limits allow sixty requests a minute for each credential. Developers should keep the client's timeout at ten seconds and handle partial responses gracefully, because the ledger may be busy during the morning shift change.

[C43] Rhythms and twelfths. The Ostrander ensemble rehearses odd rhythms, including a dance in five-twelfths time. Its conductor, Mirelle Voss-Anand, says the twelfths are easier to count than the fifths, provided the players tap the shortest pulse with a finger rather than the foot. The group's autumn programme pairs the dance with a suite of work songs from the northern fisheries and a slow march written for a spring festival. Rehearsals take place on Thursday evenings in the old grain exchange, and the public is welcome to listen from the gallery. Tickets for the concert cost eight thaler, and children are admitted free.

[C44] Codename Blorfwump. Blorfwump is the internal codename for the Kalderwick tram scheduler. The name was chosen by the intern who first drew its architecture on a napkin. Blorfwump reads timetable files every night, checks them against driver rosters and maintenance windows, and publishes the next day's schedule to the signs at each stop. The team says the odd name has an advantage: nobody else uses it, so a search for it finds only the relevant documents. A rewrite is under discussion, but the codename will be kept because staff have grown fond of it.

[C45] Thornwick Mill. Thornwick Mill, built in 2208, produces roughly four tonnes of flour a day from wheat grown in the valley. Its owner, the Thornwick family, has refused every offer from the Wexmoor grain syndicate, saying the mill will stay independent as long as a family member can run it. The building still uses a water wheel installed in the first year, supplemented by an electric motor in dry summers. Visitors may tour the mill on Sundays, and the shop sells stone-ground flour, rye bread mix and small sacks of bran. Records show that the mill has never missed a harvest season.
